identity.title: A machine-learning approach for identifying the counterparts of submillimetre galaxies and applications to the GOODS-North field
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use this ALMA sample to develop a training set suitable for machine-learning (ML) algorithms to determine how to identify SMG counterparts in multiwavelength images

question.value: Can machine-learning classifiers trained on ALMA-identified SMG counterparts in UDS identify SMG counterparts in fields lacking interferometric follow-up (GOODS-N)?

evidence.quote: We apply our trained neural network to the GOODS-North field, which also has single-dish submm observations from the S2CLS and deep multiwavelength data but little high-resolution interferometric submm imaging

method.value: SMGs from ALMA matches; non-SMGs are multiwavelength sources within 7 arcsec of SCUBA-2 sources with ALMA detections, stars removed with SExtractor classification

evidence.quote: The resulting training set for our ML testing contained a total of 1439 sources: 514 SMGs; and 925 non-SMGs

method.value: 14 features (12 magnitudes, 850 um flux, scaled angular separation); LR, SVM, RF, LDA, KNN, GNB, DT, BDT and four NNs; hyperparameters tuned by 4-fold CV on F1

evidence.quote: We chose to set $k=4$ in order to have a more reasonable computation time.

key_parameters.value: NN: 150 epochs, batch 64, ADAM lr 0.001 with time-based decay

evidence.quote: training each network for 150 epochs, with 64 samples per batch provided a good solution.
we repeated this process 50 times, thus obtaining a total of 200 estimates

method.value: Ensemble of 100 1-layer NNs, mean score cutoff 0.5

evidence.quote: training 100 NNs in parallel and taking the average and standard deviation of the resulting prediction scores.

results_numeric.quantity: GOODS-N SCUBA-2 sources with ML-identified counterpart

evidence.quote: These 45 multiwavelength ML-identified SMG candidates lie in 36 SCUBA-2 sources (out of a possible 67)
only 37 out of 1000 fake ‘beams’ contained any false positive IDs, giving a false positive of 3.7 per cent

claims.hypothesis: ML can identify SMG counterparts better than manual colour cuts
claims.experiment: Compare ML classifiers and tuned colour cuts by 4-fold CV
claims.result: NN F1 ~85.6 vs manual 81.4 per cent
claims.finding: Neural network best, but improvement is modest (~5 per cent)

evidence.quote: the improvement in using machine learning is modest (about 5 per cent)

claims.hypothesis: The UDS-trained network transfers to GOODS-N
claims.experiment: Apply ensemble NN to GOODS-N and compare with SMA and super-deblending
claims.result: 36/67 sources classified; 15 of 33 SMA detections matched

evidence.quote: This is equivalent to a matching success rate of 68 per cent and a completeness of 45 per cent.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Imputation of missing features gave no significant improvement, so only full-featured sources were used

evidence.quote: Even with this specific imputation method, we saw no significant improvement compared to removing examples with missing data.

limitations_admitted.value: Only fully featured sources classified; photometric uncertainties ignored

evidence.quote: Currently, our classification algorithm does not take into account missing features or flux density uncertainties.
